implementation_notes: JMS is the pattern's classic host: the provider owns a store, DeliveryMode.PERSISTENT is the default delivery mode and 'the most reliable way to produce a message is to send a PERSISTENT message, and to do so within a transaction'. In JMS 2.0 (Java EE 7 and later) that is a JMSContext created with JMSContext.SESSION_TRANSACTED plus context.commit(); the acknowledgement of consumed messages happens at commit of a transacted session or on message.acknowledge() in CLIENT_ACKNOWLEDGE mode, so the ack can be placed after the business commit. The classic session/consumer structure is still justified whenever the provider is the durability mechanism; it is what the language's ecosystem provides rather than something a simpler idiom replaces.
pitfalls: acknowledge() (or a session commit) before the database commit converts a crash into silent loss; rollbacks redeliver everything consumed since the last commit, so the handler must tolerate duplicates.
Explicitly setting NON_PERSISTENT - or using a provider whose 'persistent' store is only a local file without replication - silently downgrades the guarantee.
Transacted and non-transacted contexts must not be mixed for the same destination, and a context is not thread-safe; share it per thread or per unit of work.
A transacted session holds consumed messages until commit, so long processing inside one transaction grows the provider's store and can trip its limits.

variants.name: Container-managed XA/JTA transaction over DB and JMS
variants.implementation_notes: One two-phase-commit transaction spanning the database and the JMS resource makes 'business write plus send' atomic, which is as close to exactly-once as the JVM platform gets without an outbox. Annotate the service method with a REQUIRED transaction attribute and inject an XA connection factory; the container commits both resources or neither, and the provider's recovery (XAResource.recover) settles in-doubt branches after a crash. Use it when the participating resources are few and stable; where XA is unavailable or too slow, prefer the transactional-outbox shape that the JMS/JDBC combination can express with one ordinary transaction.
pitfalls: Two-phase commit is slow and can end in a heuristic outcome that only a human can resolve; long-running XA transactions amplify it.
Not every database/JMS-provider pair implements XA correctly (or at all) - verify the resource's recover() behaviour before relying on it.
The XA transaction must contain only the business work: HTTP calls, file I/O or user interaction inside it hold locks and connections.
A missing transaction manager recovery configuration leaves in-doubt branches after a crash, which is exactly the failure the variant was chosen to remove.

variants.name: Kafka transactional producer (offset and output commit together)
variants.implementation_notes: Kafka's log is the store and its transactional producer is the acknowledgement protocol: enable.idempotence=true (the default since Kafka 3.0) removes duplicates per partition, and initTransactions/beginTransaction/commitTransaction with sendOffsetsToTransaction make 'process the input record, produce the outputs, commit the consumer offset' one atomic unit, so a crash in between produces either both or neither. Choose it for stream/consume-transform-produce workloads where the input offset is the acknowledgement; consumers must read with isolation.level=read_committed, otherwise they observe records from aborted transactions.
pitfalls: A stable transactional.id is required for fencing; two instances sharing one id (or a random id per restart) either fight or lose the zombie protection.
initTransactions must run once per producer instance before any beginTransaction, and an uncommitted transaction blocks other producers on the same id until transaction.timeout.ms elapses.
Consumers that do not set read_committed see records that were later aborted, which breaks the promise the transaction was supposed to give.
Producing inside a transaction without sendOffsetsToTransaction re-reads the input after a crash and re-produces the output - the duplicate this variant exists to prevent.
